units.headline: Record metadata lookup errors are now ignored instead of failing Track
units.summary: For KindRecord items, loadMetadata now drops the getRecord error and always returns success. Track therefore stores the item with metadata that has no owner, where before it returned an error. This now happens for every error, transient connection or timeout failures included, not only FORBIDDEN replies.
focus: Transient failures such as timeouts or connection refused now make Track succeed with no owner, and nothing re-resolves the owner later
Callers of Track that relied on its error to retry or alert
Any code downstream that needs it.Owner or md.record.Owner to be set for record items

issues.title: Transient lookup failures permanently leave tracked items without owner
issues.detail: Every getRecord error is now swallowed, not just ReplyError. If the inventory server is briefly unreachable, Track still succeeds and stores Metadata with an empty Owner. Track never looks the record up again, so the item stays without an owner until it is forgotten and tracked again.
issues.failure_scenario: Inventory times out during Track(&Item{ID:"/tenants/rec-orders", Kind:KindRecord}). Track returns nil, l.meta stores a record with Owner "", and it.Owner is never set to the real owner. Before this change Track returned an error, so the caller could retry.

units.reason: Changes error handling so failures that used to reject Track now succeed with partial metadata.

units.headline: New tests for client error caching, isErrorReply and loadMetadata fallback
units.summary: Adds tests for the per-key error cache and its TTL, success caching, isErrorReply with wrapped and unwrapped errors, and loadMetadata's fallback on a FORBIDDEN reply. The fake get returns ReplyError by value, which is what Conn.Get returns. These are new tests only and cannot change production behavior.
units.reason: New test file only; it cannot change production behavior.
